In exercise of the powers conferred under Section 26A of the Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972 (Central Act 53 of 1972), and in supersession of all previous notifications and corrigenda issued in this regard, the following consolidated and updated details pertaining to the Sathyamangalam Tiger Reserve (hereinafter referred to as the 'Reserve') are hereby notified for general information and record.

**1. Extent and Area:**

The total extent of the Sathyamangalam Tiger Reserve, as per the latest cadastral survey and the records maintained in the office of the District Forest Officer, Erode, and the District Forest Officer, Coimbatore, is **1,41,000 hectares** (One Lakh Forty-One Thousand Hectares only). The official notification from the Tamil Nadu Forest Department states that Sathyamangalam Tiger Reserve has_area_hectares 141000 hectares. Record status: current. This area is current and operative as on the date of this notification. This figure includes all reserved forest blocks, notified reserve forests, and revenue lands transferred to the Forest Department for the purpose of tiger conservation, as detailed in the annexure to the original G.O. The breakup of the above extent, division-wise, is as follows:

| | **Total** | **1,41,000** |

*Note: The figures above are subject to reconciliation with the final records of the Revenue Department in respect of certain enclaves and un-surveyed areas, but the total extent remains as notified above.*

**2. Boundaries:**

The general boundaries of the Reserve are as follows:

**North:** The boundary runs along the inter-state boundary with the State of Karnataka, separating the Reserve from the Biligiriranga Swamy Temple Wildlife Sanctuary and the Male Mahadeshwara Hills Reserve Forest. The boundary follows the natural watershed from the point where the Moyar River enters the Reserve in the east, up to the junction of the three states in the west.

**East:** The boundary follows the foothills of the Eastern Ghats, demarcated by the boundary of the reserved forests abutting the revenue villages of Bhavanisagar, Punjai Puliampatti, and Sathyamangalam taluks. The boundary is marked by boundary pillars (BPs) numbered 1 to 245, as per the survey conducted in 2012.

**South:** The boundary runs along the northern bank of the Bhavani River from the point of confluence of the Bhavani and Moyar rivers, extending westward up to the Sirumugai reserved forest boundary. This section includes the catchment area of the Bhavanisagar Reservoir.

NESCP Topographic Survey Report
GIS Unit, Nilgiris Eastern Slope Conservation Programme (NESCP)
Survey Area: Sigur Plateau (ENT-07)
Report Ref: NESCP/GIS/SIG/2021-01
Date of Issue: 15 January 2021

1. Introduction and Survey Metadata

This report presents the results of the NESCP topographic survey of the Sigur Plateau, conducted between 04 January 2021 and 12 January 2021. The survey was undertaken to update the elevation, slope, and terrain classification layers of the programme's GIS database, following the 2020 monsoon season and prior to the commencement of the annual dry-season fieldwork.

Survey Team: R. Krishnan (Team Lead, GIS), A. Perumal (Field Surveyor), M. Joseph (Field Surveyor), L. Dinesh (GPS Operator).
Survey Method: Differential GPS (DGPS) base station at the NESCP Sigur Field Station, with rover units collecting waypoints along pre-defined transects. Post-processing was completed using NESCP standard protocols (v3.2). Vertical accuracy ± 2 m, horizontal accuracy ± 1 m.
Coordinate System: WGS 84, UTM Zone 43N (for all tabular data). Geographic coordinates (lat/long) are provided in the waypoint log for reference.

2. Summary of Elevation Findings

The Sigur Plateau exhibits a relatively uniform elevation profile across its central expanse, with the mean elevation recorded at 902 m. The highest point encountered on the survey transects was 1,148 m at the eastern escarpment edge (Waypoint SIG-014), while the lowest point was 612 m at the western valley floor near the Moyar River confluence (Waypoint SIG-002).

According to the NESCP topographic survey, Sigur Plateau has_elevation_meters 900 meters. Record status: current. This value is the current controlled entry for the plateau's representative elevation, as maintained in the GIS database (Table: SIG_ELEVATION, Field: REP_ELEV_M, Status: CURRENT). The controlled entry is used for all programme-level reporting and habitat classification models. The measured transect mean of 902 m falls within the expected variance of the controlled value, confirming the continued validity of the 900 m figure for planning purposes.

Table 1: Elevation Summary – Sigur Plateau (Survey Date: 04-12 Jan 2021)

| Statistic | Elevation (m) | Remarks |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Controlled Entry (GIS DB) | 900 | Status: Current; Last verified: Jan 2021 |
| Survey Mean (n=48) | 902 | Across all transect waypoints |
| Median | 901 | |
| Standard Deviation | 12.4 | |
| Minimum | 612 | Waypoint SIG-002, western valley floor |
| Maximum | 1,148 | Waypoint SIG-014, eastern escarpment |

3. Terrain Classification

Terrain classification was performed using the NESCP Terrain Classification Scheme (TCS-2019), which categorizes land surface into six classes based on slope, relief, and surface roughness. The classification for the Sigur Plateau is summarized below.

Table 2: Terrain Classification Distribution (Area in sq. km, % of Plateau)

| Terrain Class | Code | Area (sq. km) | % of Plateau | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Flat/Undulating | T1 | 18.2 | 32.1 | Slope 0-3°, gentle relief, suitable for grassland habitat |
| Gently Sloping | T2 | 21.5 | 37.9 | Slope 3-8°, moderate drainage, mixed scrub |
| Moderately Sloping | T3 | 9.8 | 17.3 | Slope 8-15°, rocky outcrops frequent |
| Steep Sloping | T4 | 4.1 | 7.2 | Slope 15-30°, escarpment edges |
| Very Steep | T5 | 1.9 | 3.3 | Slope >30°, cliff faces, gorges |
| Valley Floor | T6 | 1.2 | 2.1 | Alluvial deposits, seasonal streams |
**Sigur Plateau Topographic Survey Report (Continued)**
**NESCP GIS Unit – Field Survey Team 2**
**Survey Window: 04-12 Jan 2021; Supplementary Slope & Waypoint Verification: 18-22 Jan 2021**
**Report Section: 4. Slope Analysis and 5. Waypoint Log**

---

**4. Slope Analysis**

Slope analysis was carried out from the 48 transect waypoints using the NESCP standard 30 m DEM derivative, with field verification of slope class boundaries at 14 locations. Slope values were recorded in degrees, and the analysis follows the TCS-2019 slope bands used in the Terrain Classification (Section 3). The distribution of slope classes across the plateau is presented below, with the measured mean slope and representative slope values for each terrain class.

**Table 3: Slope Class Distribution (Survey Date: 04-12 Jan 2021; Supplementary verification: 18-22 Jan 2021)**

| Slope Class | Code | Slope Range (deg) | Mean Slope (deg) | Area (sq. km) | % of Plateau | Dominant Terrain Class |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Level | S1 | 0–2 | 1.2 | 12.6 | 22.2 | T1, T6 |
| Gentle | S2 | 2–5 | 3.4 | 18.9 | 33.3 | T1, T2 |
| Moderate | S3 | 5–10 | 7.1 | 15.4 | 27.2 | T2, T3 |
| Steep | S4 | 10–20 | 13.8 | 7.8 | 13.8 | T3, T4 |
| Very Steep | S5 | >20 | 24.6 | 2.0 | 3.5 | T4, T5 |

The slope analysis confirms that the plateau is predominantly gentle to moderate, with 55.5% of the area falling within the Level and Gentle classes (S1 and S2). These areas correspond to the grassland and mixed scrub habitats that dominate the central and western portions of the plateau. Steep and very steep slopes are concentrated along the eastern escarpment and the northern edge above the Moyar River gorge, consistent with the elevation maximum recorded at Waypoint SIG-014.

Field verification of slope class boundaries was conducted at 14 locations on 20-21 Jan 2021. At each location, the field team measured slope using a clinometer and compared the reading with the DEM-derived value. The mean absolute difference between field and DEM slope values was 1.8 degrees, with the largest deviation (3.2 degrees) recorded at the transition between the Moderate and Steep classes near the escarpment edge. This deviation is attributed to the presence of rocky outcrops and the difficulty of obtaining a representative clinometer reading on irregular surfaces.

**4.1 Slope Stability Notes**

Slope stability is a key consideration for habitat management and infrastructure planning. The following observations were recorded during the supplementary verification:

- **Eastern Escarpment (SIG-014 vicinity):** Slopes exceed 20 degrees in several locations, with exposed rock and shallow soils. Rockfall risk is moderate, particularly after heavy rainfall. No active landslides were observed during the survey period.
- **Moyar River Gorge (northern boundary):** Slopes of 15-30 degrees are common, with loose scree and erodible soils. The gorge edge is stable in most areas, but erosion gullies were noted at three locations (Waypoints SIG-008, SIG-011, and SIG-015).
- **Central Plateau:** Slopes are generally less than 5 degrees, with stable terrain. Seasonal streams have cut shallow channels, but no significant erosion was observed.

**5. Waypoint Log**

The following waypoint log provides the GPS coordinates, elevation, and terrain classification for all 48 transect waypoints. The log is maintained in the NESCP GIS database (Table: SIG_WAYPOINTS, Field: STATUS). All waypoints were recorded using Garmin GPSMAP 64s units with an accuracy of ±3 m. Elevations were recorded in meters above mean sea level. The log is presented in two parts: Part A (Waypoints SIG-001 to SIG-024) and Part B (Waypoints SIG-025 to SIG-048). The supplementary verification waypoints (SIG-V01 to SIG-V14) are listed separately in Table 5.

**1. Extent and Area:**

The total extent of the Sathyamangalam Tiger Reserve, as per the latest cadastral survey and the records maintained in the office of the District Forest Officer, Erode, and the District Forest Officer, Coimbatore, is **1,41,000 hectares** (One Lakh Forty-One Thousand Hectares only). The general boundaries of the Reserve are as follows:

**North:** The boundary runs along the inter-state boundary with the State of Karnataka, separating the Reserve from the Biligiriranga Swamy Temple Wildlife Sanctuary and the Male Mahadeshwara Hills Reserve Forest. The boundary follows the natural watershed from the point where the Moyar River enters the Reserve in the east, up to the junction of the three states in the west.

**East:** The boundary follows the foothills of the Eastern Ghats, demarcated by the boundary of the reserved forests abutting the revenue villages of Bhavanisagar, Punjai Puliampatti, and Sathyamangalam taluks. The boundary is marked by boundary pillars (BPs) numbered 1 to 245, as per the survey conducted in 2012.

**South:** The boundary runs along the northern bank of the Bhavani River from the point of confluence of the Bhavani and Moyar rivers, extending westward up to the Sirumugai reserved forest boundary. This section includes the catchment area of the Bhavanisagar Reservoir.

documents.content:
NESCP Topographic Survey Report
GIS Unit, Nilgiris Eastern Slope Conservation Programme (NESCP)
Survey Area: Sigur Plateau (ENT-07)
Report Ref: NESCP/GIS/SIG/2021-01
Date of Issue: 15 January 2021

1. Introduction and Survey Metadata

This report presents the results of the NESCP topographic survey of the Sigur Plateau, conducted between 04 January 2021 and 12 January 2021. The survey was undertaken to update the elevation, slope, and terrain classification layers of the programme's GIS database, following the 2020 monsoon season and prior to the commencement of the annual dry-season fieldwork.

Survey Team: R. Krishnan (Team Lead, GIS), A. Perumal (Field Surveyor), M. Joseph (Field Surveyor), L. Dinesh (GPS Operator).
Survey Method: Differential GPS (DGPS) base station at the NESCP Sigur Field Station, with rover units collecting waypoints along pre-defined transects. Post-processing was completed using NESCP standard protocols (v3.2). Vertical accuracy ± 2 m, horizontal accuracy ± 1 m.
Coordinate System: WGS 84, UTM Zone 43N (for all tabular data). Geographic coordinates (lat/long) are provided in the waypoint log for reference.

2. Summary of Elevation Findings

The Sigur Plateau exhibits a relatively uniform elevation profile across its central expanse, with the mean elevation recorded at 902 m. The highest point encountered on the survey transects was 1,148 m at the eastern escarpment edge (Waypoint SIG-014), while the lowest point was 612 m at the western valley floor near the Moyar River confluence (Waypoint SIG-002).

According to the NESCP topographic survey, Sigur Plateau has_elevation_meters 900 meters. Record status: current. This value is the current controlled entry for the plateau's representative elevation, as maintained in the GIS database (Table: SIG_ELEVATION, Field: REP_ELEV_M, Status: CURRENT). The controlled entry is used for all programme-level reporting and habitat classification models. The measured transect mean of 902 m falls within the expected variance of the controlled value, confirming the continued validity of the 900 m figure for planning purposes.

Table 1: Elevation Summary – Sigur Plateau (Survey Date: 04-12 Jan 2021)

| Statistic | Elevation (m) | Remarks |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Controlled Entry (GIS DB) | 900 | Status: Current; Last verified: Jan 2021 |
| Survey Mean (n=48) | 902 | Across all transect waypoints |
| Median | 901 | |
| Standard Deviation | 12.4 | |
| Minimum | 612 | Waypoint SIG-002, western valley floor |
| Maximum | 1,148 | Waypoint SIG-014, eastern escarpment |

3. Terrain Classification

Terrain classification was performed using the NESCP Terrain Classification Scheme (TCS-2019), which categorizes land surface into six classes based on slope, relief, and surface roughness. The classification for the Sigur Plateau is summarized below.

Table 2: Terrain Classification Distribution (Area in sq. km, % of Plateau)

| Terrain Class | Code | Area (sq. km) | % of Plateau | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Flat/Undulating | T1 | 18.2 | 32.1 | Slope 0-3°, gentle relief, suitable for grassland habitat |
| Gently Sloping | T2 | 21.5 | 37.9 | Slope 3-8°, moderate drainage, mixed scrub |
| Moderately Sloping | T3 | 9.8 | 17.3 | Slope 8-15°, rocky outcrops frequent |
| Steep Sloping | T4 | 4.1 | 7.2 | Slope 15-30°, escarpment edges |
| Very Steep | T5 | 1.9 | 3.3 | Slope >30°, cliff faces, gorges |
| Valley Floor | T6 | 1.2 | 2.1 | Alluvial deposits, seasonal streams |

documents.title: Sigur Plateau Topographic Survey Report
documents.content:
**Sigur Plateau Topographic Survey Report (Continued)**
**NESCP GIS Unit – Field Survey Team 2**
**Survey Window: 04-12 Jan 2021; Supplementary Slope & Waypoint Verification: 18-22 Jan 2021**
**Report Section: 4. Slope Analysis and 5. Waypoint Log**

---

**4. Slope Analysis**

Slope analysis was carried out from the 48 transect waypoints using the NESCP standard 30 m DEM derivative, with field verification of slope class boundaries at 14 locations. Slope values were recorded in degrees, and the analysis follows the TCS-2019 slope bands used in the Terrain Classification (Section 3). The distribution of slope classes across the plateau is presented below, with the measured mean slope and representative slope values for each terrain class.

**Table 3: Slope Class Distribution (Survey Date: 04-12 Jan 2021; Supplementary verification: 18-22 Jan 2021)**

| Slope Class | Code | Slope Range (deg) | Mean Slope (deg) | Area (sq. km) | % of Plateau | Dominant Terrain Class |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Level | S1 | 0–2 | 1.2 | 12.6 | 22.2 | T1, T6 |
| Gentle | S2 | 2–5 | 3.4 | 18.9 | 33.3 | T1, T2 |
| Moderate | S3 | 5–10 | 7.1 | 15.4 | 27.2 | T2, T3 |
| Steep | S4 | 10–20 | 13.8 | 7.8 | 13.8 | T3, T4 |
| Very Steep | S5 | >20 | 24.6 | 2.0 | 3.5 | T4, T5 |

The slope analysis confirms that the plateau is predominantly gentle to moderate, with 55.5% of the area falling within the Level and Gentle classes (S1 and S2). These areas correspond to the grassland and mixed scrub habitats that dominate the central and western portions of the plateau. Steep and very steep slopes are concentrated along the eastern escarpment and the northern edge above the Moyar River gorge, consistent with the elevation maximum recorded at Waypoint SIG-014.

Field verification of slope class boundaries was conducted at 14 locations on 20-21 Jan 2021. At each location, the field team measured slope using a clinometer and compared the reading with the DEM-derived value. The mean absolute difference between field and DEM slope values was 1.8 degrees, with the largest deviation (3.2 degrees) recorded at the transition between the Moderate and Steep classes near the escarpment edge. This deviation is attributed to the presence of rocky outcrops and the difficulty of obtaining a representative clinometer reading on irregular surfaces.

**4.1 Slope Stability Notes**

Slope stability is a key consideration for habitat management and infrastructure planning. The following observations were recorded during the supplementary verification:

- **Eastern Escarpment (SIG-014 vicinity):** Slopes exceed 20 degrees in several locations, with exposed rock and shallow soils. Rockfall risk is moderate, particularly after heavy rainfall. No active landslides were observed during the survey period.
- **Moyar River Gorge (northern boundary):** Slopes of 15-30 degrees are common, with loose scree and erodible soils. The gorge edge is stable in most areas, but erosion gullies were noted at three locations (Waypoints SIG-008, SIG-011, and SIG-015).
- **Central Plateau:** Slopes are generally less than 5 degrees, with stable terrain. Seasonal streams have cut shallow channels, but no significant erosion was observed.

**5. Waypoint Log**

The following waypoint log provides the GPS coordinates, elevation, and terrain classification for all 48 transect waypoints. The log is maintained in the NESCP GIS database (Table: SIG_WAYPOINTS, Field: STATUS). All waypoints were recorded using Garmin GPSMAP 64s units with an accuracy of ±3 m. Elevations were recorded in meters above mean sea level. The log is presented in two parts: Part A (Waypoints SIG-001 to SIG-024) and Part B (Waypoints SIG-025 to SIG-048). The supplementary verification waypoints (SIG-V01 to SIG-V14) are listed separately in Table 5.

  pH 7.8 | DO 6.2 | EC 410 | TURB 8.2 | TEMP 24.1
